properties.title: Temporal Flow Matching for Learning Spatio-Temporal Trajectories in 4D Longitudinal Medical Imaging

membership.reason: Implements a learned 4D spatio-temporal Flow Matching ODE transition (v_theta) that transports filled longitudinal 3D medical image history to a future target 3D scan.

properties.backbone: TorchCFM Attention UNet predicting velocity field v_theta(X_tau, tau) at full spatial resolution

properties.flow: Sparse 3D scan sequence I -> Sparsity Filling I' -> Flow Matching ODE integration v_theta -> Mean/last predicted target 3D scan I_hat_target

properties.purpose: Future 3D medical image prediction from sparse/irregular longitudinal scans (cardiac Cine-MRI, stroke perfusion CT, glioma MRI).

assertions.rationale: Missing context frames are explicitly represented and handled via Sparsity Filling (replacing missing frames with nearest available scan).
Handles irregular/sparse follow-ups via dimension padding and Sparsity Filling.
Maintains full-resolution 4D spatio-temporal state tensor X_tau in R^{T x D x H x W} transported along ODE flow from context I' to target.
Conditions prediction on the entire filled multi-timepoint context sequence I'.
Jointly processes T context frames via spatio-temporal UNet with cross-attention.
Autonomous observation-to-observation forecasting without settable treatment or control actions.
Models temporal evolution from context scans to future target scan.
Learned velocity field v_theta(X_tau, tau) integrated via ODE solver.
No action conditioning in the velocity field v_theta(X_tau, tau).
Deterministic ODE integration from filled context I' (stochastic SDE sampling is explicitly listed as future work on p. 8).
Directly outputs full-resolution 3D volumetric medical images.
Evaluates next-target 3D scan prediction (NRMSE, SSIM, PSNR) across ACDC, ISLES, and Lumiere test sets (Table 2).
No planner or policy coupled to TFM.
Longitudinal disease progression, cardiac motion, and tumor growth imaging prediction.
Paper states 'Code will be published at https://github.com/MIC-DKFZ/Temporal-Flow-Matching' (not verified live).
Table 2 reports NRMSE, SSIM, and PSNR over 3 runs on held-out test sets for ACDC, ISLES, and Lumiere.
Figure 3 evaluates zero-shot robustness to progressive masking of early (1->T) and late (T->1) context frames.

this fundamental gap, we introduce Temporal Flow Match-

dimension as a fixed input dimension. With this, we propose
Temporal Flow Matching(TFM), a generative model that
directly learns transformations from each context image to
the target image within a unified spatio-temporal flow for-
mulation. Unlike approaches that compress temporal infor-
mation early, or operate on latent representation, TFM re-
tains full spatial resolution. This is feasible because TFM
has a computational footprint comparable to other spatio-
temporal methods, which makes it able to afford this mod-
eling compute. By jointly processing the entire input se-
quence, the model can leverage spatio-temporal dependen-
cies between input images. To enable this, we define the

To address missing context images, we apply sparsity filling, replacing them with the most recent available scan (see Fig. 2 for visualization). This ensures smoother inputs and more stable flow estimation across masked inputs. If missing frames occur before the first available scan, we fill them using the earliest available image. We denote the filled context sequence via I ′.

ACDC [3] is a cardiac MRI dataset for different states
of the heart. Images are reshaped to [T, H, D, W] =
[11, 32, 128, 128], where the target is a single image hav-
ing the same spatial dimensions. For the ACDC dataset, we
randomly mask out time points, in order to make it irregu-
lar. We split the dataset into 80 training, 20 validation and
50 test images. This dataset was used for method develop-
ment and ablations were done on the validation set.
[paraphrase (visual p.7)] Table 3 ablates Att UNet & Mean (NRMSE 0.0261, SSIM 96.04%, PSNR 32.30) vs No Att: Mean (0.0270), No Sparsity Filling (0.0444), and LCI+FM* (0.1029) on ACDC validation set.

• Explicit Continuous Time Modeling While our current
setting treats τ as abstract interpolation scalars, this can
be naturally extended to model continuous, real-valued
time steps. This would allow for more flexible predic-
tions, ideal for clinical workflows.
• Stochastic Generation It is technically simple to include
stochastic sampling into TFM. This would allow TFM to
sample multiple possible futures. This could be again
valuable in the clinical context for risk assessment and
planning. On a technical level, this only requires extend-
ing the ODE to SDE integration and adding noise during
training (see step (6)1).

capability_assessments.rationale: Implements learned Flow Matching ODE transition over longitudinal 3D medical image sequences and evaluates next-target scan prediction on ACDC, ISLES, and Lumiere without action conditioning.

limitations: Table 2 SimVP row on ISLES (0.124 / 52.8 / 21.21) is identical to ACDC, indicating a likely copy-paste typo in the paper.
Real-valued continuous time steps and stochastic sampling are not implemented (explicitly deferred to future work, p. 8).
notes: All 12 physical PDF pages read; Figures 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 visually inspected.

legacy_cells.B: Temporal Flow Matching for Learning Spatio-Temporal Trajectories in 4D Longitudinal Medical Imaging
legacy_cells.C: Disch, Nico Albert, Kirchhoff, Yannick, Peretzke, Robin, Rokuss, Maximilian, Roy, Saikat, Ulrich, Constantin, et al.
legacy_cells.O: Cardiac MRI (ACDC heart states/pathologies); glioma/glioblastoma longitudinal MRI (LUMIERE); stroke perfusion CT (ISLES 2024).
legacy_cells.S: Given a patient's prior medical image sequence, predict the target/future 3D medical image.
legacy_cells.T: Patients represented in ACDC cardiac MRI, LUMIERE glioma MRI, and ISLES 2024 stroke perfusion CT; eligibility criteria are not specified in the extracted methods.
legacy_cells.AI: 3D longitudinal medical image volumes: cardiac MRI (ACDC); glioma MRI (LUMIERE); perfusion CT (ISLES 2024).
legacy_cells.AJ: UNet velocity-field network, with cross-attention between time embeddings and spatial feature maps.
legacy_cells.AN: Sparsity filling: replace missing context images with the most recent available scan; before the first available scan, use the earliest available image.
legacy_cells.BL: Inference uses 10 ODE integration steps (FM interpolation parameter τ from 0 to 1); no clinical-time step size is specified.
legacy_cells.BS: Predicted target 3D medical image volume; inference reduces the predicted temporal dimension using the last predicted time channel or the mean across time.
legacy_cells.BV: Flow-matching velocity loss: squared discrepancy between the predicted velocity field and the target velocity (target-minus-filled-context images); optimized with AdamW.
legacy_cells.DQ: ACDC: 80 training, 20 validation, 50 test images; ISLES: 92 training, 23 validation, 34 test images; LUMIERE: 48 training, 12 validation, 14 test images.
legacy_cells.DX: Test-set image prediction metrics reported: normalized RMSE (NRMSE), SSIM [%], and PSNR; the paper states TFM outperforms LCI across all datasets and metrics. Table 2's extracted row alignment is unclear, so no dataset-specific values are transcribed.
legacy_cells.EG: Inference uses 10 ODE integration steps; the authors report that one function evaluation significantly reduces performance and that gains become marginal beyond five evaluations on one ACDC validation set.
legacy_cells.EI: Compared with non-WM image-prediction baselines LCI, ConvLSTM, SimVP, and ViViT; authors report TFM outperforms LCI across all datasets and metrics.
legacy_cells.EK: Ablations: attention UNet vs no-attention UNet; mean vs last-frame aggregation; removal of sparsity filling; single-context LCI + FM.
legacy_cells.EL: ViViT on LUMIERE ran out of 40GB memory; without sparsity filling training was unstable/degraded; single-context LCI + FM showed poor performance and unstable training; SimVP produced negative SSIM and qualitatively noisy results on LUMIERE.
legacy_cells.FB: Full-resolution 3D image/voxel trajectory: a stack of context volumes is transformed toward repeated target volumes, with the network predicting image-space flow/differences.
legacy_cells.FL: Image volumes (context) → image-space interpolation state Xτ → UNet velocity-field network with time/spatial cross-attention → ODE integration → target image volume; no planner.
legacy_cells.FM: Introduces Temporal Flow Matching for full-resolution 3D longitudinal image prediction using multiple, sparse/irregular context scans; proposes Difference Modeling and sparsity filling; benchmarks against spatio-temporal methods on ACDC, ISLES, and LUMIERE.
legacy_cells.FN: Authors report TFM outperforms LCI across all datasets and metrics and achieves top performance on each tested dataset/metric; image metrics include NRMSE, SSIM, and PSNR.
legacy_cells.FO: The authors cite scarcity of large, high-quality follow-up cohorts; global fixed-resolution sampling may miss localized details; data scarcity challenges conventional baselines; pretrained resources are not readily available.
legacy_cells.FP: Future work includes learned imputation or temporal interpolation priors, explicit continuous clinical-time modeling, stochastic generation, localized/patch-based modeling, and pretrained models fine-tuned for 4D prediction.
legacy_cells.FQ: Authors identify that most deep-learning methods analyze isolated time points or focus on classification/regression, while longitudinal imaging methods are technically constrained or disease-specific.
legacy_cells.FR: Evidence supports retrospective prediction of a target medical image from prior images, not treatment-effect identification, counterfactual treatment comparison, planning, clinical decision utility, or prospective benefit.
legacy_cells.FS: Reviewer mapping: M3 Belief-state service; M5 Dynamics adapter; M7 Outcome & causal layer
legacy_cells.FT: Reviewer lesson: Expose future-state forecasts through a time-aware dynamics interface and validate error versus horizon; treatment actions need separate evidence before intervention simulation.
legacy_cells.FX: Read all 12 pages of the complete extracted PDF text: title/abstract and introduction (pp. 1–2); methods, equations, and Algorithm 1 (pp. 3–5); dataset and experimental setup (p. 6); results, Tables 2–3, and masking figure (p. 7); discussion, limitations, conclusion, and future work (p. 8); references and appendices A–D including Table 4 (pp. 9–12). | Codex audit: title/byline, abstract/conclusion, targeted methods/results and cross-check of prior quotations against extracted full text. This is a targeted audit, not an independent re-extraction of every negative/unreported field.
legacy_cells.FZ: A:I were left untouched. No dataset-specific Table 2 metric values were transcribed because extracted table row alignment is ambiguous. The text extraction has line-wrap/OCR artifacts in equations and tables, but the relevant narrative, methods, and dataset splits were readable. TFM predicts one target image from context; its numerical ODE integration is not treated as multi-step clinical-time rollout. Authors' broad claims about clinical relevance are not evidence of treatment-effect identification or clinical utility. Evidence QA: 28/72 populated fields had a <=25-word quotation matching extracted PDF text (38.9%). Confidence is conservative; review this row where exact quote checks were incomplete. Codex audit: 62 prior populated fields have a located source quotation; 10 have quotations not located by normalized text matching. Unlocated quotations are review flags, not proof that the value is false. Companion evidence audit lists affected columns. Reviewer FS/FT/FU mappings are synthesis.
